compiled:
📰 General

Senate Defense Bill Includes Pressure on Pentagon Over Venezuela Strikes •

The Senate passed a $901 billion defense policy bill on Wednesday, incorporating a provision demanding video evidence of recent strikes in Venezuela. The measure aims to hold Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accountable for operations targeting alleged drug trafficking organizations. The bill specifically requests photographic and video documentation of the attacks, citing concerns about transparency and the scope of U.S. involvement. Lawmakers are seeking clarification regarding the nature and legality of the military actions.

🌍 World

Nobel Laureate Machado Departs Norway Following Ceremony in Oslo •

María Corina Machado, the Venezuelan opposition leader and recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize, has departed from Oslo, Norway, following the ceremony. Her spokesperson confirmed her departure, stating that the decision was made after discussions with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre. The departure occurred after the award presentation, and details regarding her immediate plans remain unconfirmed. Security concerns reportedly played a role in the decision to leave the country.

🦅 US

Warner Bros. Discovery Urges Investors to Reject Paramount’s Hostile Bid •

Warner Bros. Discovery’s board of directors has advised shareholders to vote against Paramount’s recent hostile takeover proposal. The recommendation follows a detailed review of the offer by the company’s leadership. The board cited concerns regarding the financial viability and strategic alignment of the combined entity. Paramount, backed by the Ellison family, initially proposed a deal to create a media giant. This rejection marks a significant setback in Paramount’s attempt to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery.

💰 Business

Federal Government Cancels $285 Million Contract for Durham Chip Manufacturing Institute •

The U.S. federal government has terminated a $285 million contract awarded to the Smart USA Institute for a chip manufacturing institute based in Durham, North Carolina. The decision was communicated to the company on December 10th, citing unspecified reasons for the funding withdrawal. The institute was slated to begin construction of the facility with the intended completion date set for December 2025. The exact rationale behind the termination remains undisclosed at this time.

💻 Technology

Facebook Tests Link Posting Limits for Business Accounts – Meta Verified Required •

Meta is currently conducting a test where professional accounts and Facebook pages are limited in the number of links they can post. The experiment, observed over the past week, targets accounts without a Meta Verified subscription. This restriction applies to link sharing across the platform’s business pages. Meta’s rationale behind the test remains unclear, though it’s speculated to manage content volume and potentially encourage paid subscriptions. The change is currently limited to a test group and its long-term impact is yet to be determined.

🎭 Entertainment

Gil Gerard, ‘Buck Rogers’ Star, Passes Away at 82 After Long Battle •

Actor Gil Gerard, famed for his role as Buck Rogers in the 1970s television series, died on Tuesday at the age of 82. His wife, Janet Gerard, confirmed his passing in a Facebook post, stating he died in hospice care. Gerard’s portrayal of Buck Rogers helped popularize the science fiction character and the series achieved significant ratings during its run. The cause of death has not been publicly disclosed at this time.

🏅 Sports

Tyreek Hill Reacts to Tua Tagovailoa’s Benching with Cryptic GIF •

Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill responded to reports of quarterback Tua Tagovailoa being benched by sharing a GIF. The GIF depicts a man flashing the peace sign before seemingly vanishing. This reaction follows news of the Dolphins’ decision, which has sparked immediate speculation among fans and analysts. The exact nature of Hill’s response remains unclear, but it highlights the unusual circumstances surrounding the quarterback’s future with the team.

🔬 Science

Kīlauea Volcano Shows Activity at South Vent, North Vent Remains Quiet •

Observations from Wednesday, December 17th, indicate continued activity at the Kīlauea volcano’s south vent, characterized by regular periods of glow. Low visibility conditions significantly hampered observation efforts at the north vent, preventing identification of any glow. Seismic monitoring recorded pronounced tremor bursts occurring every 3-12 minutes. Scientists continue to monitor the volcano’s behavior closely, focusing on the south vent’s activity.

🩺 Health

Veteran Medical Editor Dr. Timothy Johnson Announces Prostate Cancer Diagnosis •

Dr. Timothy Johnson, a long-time medical editor for WCVB and ABC News, has revealed he is undergoing treatment for prostate cancer. The 89-year-old received the diagnosis following a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test. Johnson is currently undergoing treatment, details of which have not been disclosed. He shared the news publicly on “Good Morning America” as part of a broader discussion about health awareness.
